notes:
Summary: Verdant builds post-call briefs for enterprise contact centers (Zendesk + Twilio). Looking to replace a brittle homegrown summarizer. Wants: concise QA notes, coaching highlights, auto-ticket creation, and function/tool-calls to fetch CRM context.

Key requirements (customer quotes interleaved):
- "95th percentile latency for short summaries must be <450ms on average routing path" (they measure token-to-first-summary).
- Must survive seasonal spikes (Black Friday-like 8x bursts) with graceful degradation.
- Data residency: transcripts for EU customers must remain in region.
- Audit trail + immutable transcript retention 7 years for regulated customers.
- SSO/SAML + SCIM + enterprise provisioning required.

Technical preferences and constraints:
- Open to 7B/13B quantized variants for cost reasons; will accept smaller model fallback for non-critical flows.
- Wants automatic tool-calling to open Zendesk ticket with summarized transcript + suggested labels.
- Prefers routing policy: 1) dedicated capacity for peak, 2) hosted fallback for overflow, 3) lightweight model for background ticketing.
- Store raw transcripts in their S3 with server-side encryption; summaries stored in Verdant DB; Redwood must support KMS integration.

POC notes / outcomes so far:
- Integration: Twilio webhook -> ingestion -> Redwood hosted/edge for summarization -> callback to Verdant. Works end-to-end but latency spikes during sustained 5x load.
- Quality: Coaching highlights extraction works for scripted calls; struggles with multi-speaker interruptions. Need better diarization or speaker-role signals.
- Cost sensitivity: they estimate 10M tokens/month at scale; interested in Optimize recommendations (batching, KV cache, quantization) to reduce unit cost.

Stated blockers: SOC2 controls they can't waive; Procurement requires an enterprise pricing worksheet; technical team wants a follow-up stress test with realistic traffic (3/10).

Action items assigned:
- Diego: deliver tuned model config for conversational summarization + diarization tips (by 3/03).
- Nora: provide detailed pricing worksheet and draft SOW.
- Priya: coordinate legal questions re: DPA changes and data residency language.

Customer sentiment: cautiously optimistic — likes Redwood's routing/fallback story but wants concrete evidence we can meet latency & residency SLAs under spikes.

Snippets from calls: "We need the coach highlights to be push-ready — manager opens a card and gets 3 bullets + recommended remediation steps"; "If a backlog happens, we can accept delayed low-priority tickets but agent-facing summaries must stay realtime."
